solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Handy Tube serving Lakeside Co-op

indicators.note: food being served is dished up and arranged on the plate, so these letters are set out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written, twelve letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A convenient Underground line runs out to a cooperative store by a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' invites thoughts of the London Underground, but the definition is a tube you hold in your hand and look through.
explanation.definitionFit: The toy is a cylinder held up to the eye, whose mirrors turn loose coloured pieces into shifting patterns.

clue.text: Section of mounted trek can kill old horse specialist

indicators.note: a section is only a part, so the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
in a down clue, something mounted climbs upward, so the letters read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run backwards across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A cavalry trek proves so gruelling it might finish off an ageing horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'trek can kill' upward and the answer appears spanning all three words. A knacker's yard is where worn-out horses are slaughtered.
explanation.definitionFit: A knacker is a tradesman who buys worn-out horses and slaughters them for meat, hide and glue.

clue.text: Heading to where the wind blows, pull fish up

definitions.text: Heading to where the wind blows

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to draw is to pull
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler, steering downwind, hauls a catch aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces join first and the whole run is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeward describes the side or direction facing away from the wind, toward which the breeze carries things.

clue.text: Dropping an ecstasy tablet, Joe Biden is drunk; it’s a DC crime!

indicators.note: something dropped is let go, so those letters are left out
a drunk staggers about out of line, so the letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is slang for an ecstasy pill; one E is removed

explanation.surface: A US president is caught after taking a pill and getting drunk, a scandal in Washington DC.
explanation.walkthrough: DC looks like Washington, but here it is a Detective Constable, a junior British police officer. Remove one E from the name before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: An inside job is a robbery or fraud done with help from someone within the organisation, the sort a detective investigates.

clue.text: Like a mineral Perthshire town mine left abandoned?

indicators.note: what is abandoned is deserted and gone, so those letters disappear from the word

blocks.note: a small resort town in Perthshire, Scotland
a pit is a coal mine; it is removed
L is the standard abbreviation for left; it is removed

explanation.surface: A Scottish town's old mine has been left derelict, its rocks mineral-stained.
explanation.walkthrough: Pitlochry is a Highland town in Perthshire, Scotland. Strip the mine and the L from its front.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is an earthy iron-oxide mineral pigment, and ochry means resembling or containing it.

clue.text: Charles Lawrence’s empty laugh

indicators.note: an emptied word has its insides scooped out, leaving only its two ends

blocks.note: Chuck is a familiar form of Charles
only the first and last letters of the name

explanation.surface: A man called Charles Lawrence gives a hollow laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: The name reads like one person, but it splits in two: a nickname, then a surname gutted to its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A chuckle is a quiet, suppressed bout of laughter, a mild form of laughing.

clue.text: Administers toxin to revolutionary spy island captured

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the letters run the other way
a captive is held inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: to snoop is to spy; read backwards
IS is an abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A rebel agent is caught on an island and dosed with poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary spy' reads as a rebel agent, but 'revolutionary' simply turns the next word round.
explanation.definitionFit: To poison someone is to give them a toxic substance, the very act described.

clue.text: Old-fashioned, unfeeling, vacuous emperor, perhaps 49

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word keeps only its outside letters

blocks.note: square means conventional, out of date
numb means without feeling
only the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A list of insults for a dull, empty-headed ruler, followed by a strange number.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: 49 is seven times seven, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Forty-nine is seven multiplied by itself, so it is one instance of an integer that is the product of another with itself.

clue.text: With a trembling voice, sings notes

blocks.note: first meaning: the verb for singing or speaking shakily
second meaning: musical notes each half a crotchet long

explanation.walkthrough: The surface paints a nervous singer; the last word is a separate noun meaning, a type of short musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for wobbling vocally and a plural noun for eighth notes in British musical terminology.

clue.text: Hospital over-exploiting case

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for over
using someone is exploiting them

explanation.surface: A hospital takes advantage of a patient's situation, a legal case of overreach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over-exploiting' looks like one hyphenated word, but it splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A housing is a protective casing or cover around machinery or parts, like the case of a watch.

clue.text: They help to waterproof shed Sturgeon ordered

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Nicola Sturgeon, the former Scottish First Minister, orders a garden shed to be made weatherproof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as Sturgeon giving an instruction; it is the signal to rearrange the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsheets are waterproof sheets laid on the ground under a tent or sleeping bag to keep damp out.

clue.text: A week on vacation with a principally rebellious daughter? Tricky

indicators.note: a vacated place has been emptied, so only the outside letters remain
principally means chiefly or first of all, so the leading letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the word emptied to its ends
W is the abbreviation for with
taken as written
its first letter
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A week's holiday with a rebellious daughter sounds like hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' suggests a holiday, but it means the word is vacated, emptied of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricky and awkward both describe something difficult to handle or deal with smoothly.

clue.text: Artist casually greeting fellow artist Jeff (mostly ordinary)

indicators.note: most but not all, so the last letter is cut away

blocks.note: yo is a slangy, informal hello
Jeff Koons, the American artist known for balloon-dog sculptures, minus his final letter
O is the abbreviation for ordinary

explanation.surface: One artist says a casual hello to another, Jeff Koons, who is fairly unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeff Koons is the American artist behind the giant balloon-dog sculptures; drop his surname's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoko Ono is a Japanese conceptual and performance artist, also known as John Lennon's widow.

clue.text: Blundered about, turning embarrassed

indicators.note: to turn round is to face the other way, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: re means about or concerning; read backwards
red-faced with embarrassment

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles around making mistakes and goes red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blundered about' reads as one phrase meaning stumbling around, but 'about' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, so the past tense matches having made a blunder.

clue.text: Member of famous rock group associated with Airplane?

definitions.text: Member of famous rock group associated with Airplane?

blocks.clueFragment: Member of famous rock group associated with Airplane?
blocks.note: surface reading: a musician in the 1960s San Francisco band whose name pairs with Airplane
setter's reading: the presidents carved into the rock of Mount Rushmore, one of whom shares the band's first word

explanation.walkthrough: The rock group is literally rock: four presidents carved into Mount Rushmore. One of them also gave his name to the band Jefferson Airplane.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Jefferson, the third US president, is one of the four faces sculpted on Mount Rushmore in South Dakota.

clue.text: Possibly cover Dane’s film broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it widely, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A Danish director's film is shown on television, perhaps a cover version.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a cricket fielding position, the area to the off side of the batsman; the fielder stationed there is the answer, hence 'Possibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, cover is a position on the field, and the player stationed there is one example of a fielder.

clue.text: International body’s board admits European note “indefensible”

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the United Nations
a board is a table, as in bed and board
E is the abbreviation for European
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A UN committee lets in a European memo declaring some position impossible to defend.
explanation.walkthrough: The European and note pieces go together inside the board, right after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An untenable position is one that cannot be held or maintained against attack or argument.

clue.text: Physically abuse arsonist, reportedly

indicators.note: what is reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is the sound that counts

blocks.note: an arsonist is someone who torches buildings

explanation.surface: Reports claim an arsonist was beaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the two words sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To torture is to inflict severe physical pain on someone, the extreme of physical abuse.

clue.text: Number One skier drops kilo, yet has added volume

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; read as 'having added volume'

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it fall away, so a letter goes

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
the Roman numeral one
the word with its K removed
K is the abbreviation for kilo, as in the phonetic alphabet; removed

explanation.surface: The world's top skier loses weight but somehow gains bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' looks like bulk or size, but it is loudness.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with more volume in the sense of loudness is louder, which is to say more noisy.

clue.text: Infuriates five former partners

blocks.note: V is the Roman numeral five
exes are former spouses or partners

explanation.surface: Someone is driven mad by their five ex-spouses.
explanation.walkthrough: Two plain pieces: a Roman numeral, then the everyday word for former spouses or partners.
explanation.definitionFit: To vex is to annoy or irritate, so infuriating someone is a strong form of the same.

clue.text: 6 small companies start to export rayon material

indicators.note: the start of anything is its beginning, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: the Roman numeral six
S is the abbreviation for small
Cos is the abbreviation for companies
its first letter

explanation.surface: Six small firms begin shipping rayon fabric overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The 6 is a plain number here, not a reference to clue 6.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscose is a semi-synthetic fibre made from cellulose and is the commonest form of rayon fabric.

clue.text: Kiss sex god, initially ignoring serious dryness of the skin

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: X is a kiss at the end of a letter
Eros is the Greek god of love and desire
the first letters of both words

explanation.surface: A kiss from a sex god, at first brushed off, turns out to be serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignoring' looks like a deletion signal, but it is just one of the two words whose initials are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Xerosis is the medical term for abnormally dry skin, from the Greek xeros meaning dry.

clue.text: Dickens claims wizard discovered composer

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so one piece is held inside another
dis-covered means with its covering taken off, so the outer letters go

blocks.note: Boz was the pen name Charles Dickens used early in his career
Merlin, the Arthurian wizard, with its outer letters stripped

explanation.surface: Charles Dickens says a wizard found a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wizard' suggests the Wizard of Oz, but Merlin is wanted, uncovered; Dickens wrote as Boz.
explanation.definitionFit: Hector Berlioz was a French Romantic composer, best known for the Symphonie fantastique.

clue.text: Relating to area regular characters in ZZ Top neatly trimmed?

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
a trimmed beard has bits cut away, so the unwanted letters are cut away

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Asking whether the famously long-bearded rock band ZZ Top ever get a neat trim.
explanation.walkthrough: ZZ Top are an American rock trio famous for their very long beards, which makes the question mark a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Zonal means relating to or divided into zones, and a zone is a defined region or district.

clue.text: Crave English potato variety

blocks.note: to crave is to desire
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Longing for a particular English spud.
explanation.walkthrough: Desiree is a red-skinned potato cultivar common in British shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiree is a named red-skinned cultivar of potato, grown widely in Britain.

clue.text: Using Euro in northern part of France

indicators.note: using something means working or manipulating it, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Paying with euros somewhere in the north of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern part of France' reads as one phrase, but the place is far from northern: it is an island in the Indian Ocean, and it does use the euro.
explanation.definitionFit: Réunion is an overseas department of France, an island east of Madagascar, so it is fully part of the country.

clue.text: Shutdown time for today’s satellite viewing?

definitions.text: Shutdown time for today’s satellite viewing?

blocks.clueFragment: Shutdown time for today’s satellite viewing?
blocks.note: surface reading: when a satellite television service is switched off for the day
setter's reading: the natural satellite of this day, which can no longer be watched once it drops below the horizon

explanation.walkthrough: 'Satellite viewing' suggests satellite TV; the satellite is Earth's own, and viewing it ends when it sinks out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the moment the Moon disappears below the horizon, after which it cannot be observed that day.

clue.text: Blair (New Labour), half crackers, how to miss the big picture!

definitions.text: how to miss the big picture

indicators.note: to labour is to work, and worked material gets reshaped into a different form
half of something is left once the rest is gone, so only part of the word stays

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the second half of the word

explanation.surface: Tony Blair, leader of New Labour, half mad, ignoring the wider view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Labour' looks like the party's name, but 'New' is fodder and 'Labour' the signal to rework it with 'Blair'. Blinkers are leather flaps that block a horse's side vision.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing blinkers is an idiom for having a narrow outlook and ignoring everything except what lies directly ahead.
